question: Hungary has reportedly granted political asylum to former Polish Minister of Justice Zbigniew Ziobro, whom Hungarian authorities have described as being ‘politically persecuted’. Mr Ziobro is currently under indictment in Poland on 26 criminal charges. Such a decision is unprecedented within the EU.

EU law is founded on the presumption that all Member States respect the rule of law, democracy and fundamental rights, as set out in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU). This presumption underpins the principle of mutual trust, which is essential to judicial cooperation in criminal matters, including the European Arrest Warrant, under Article 82(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

Granting political asylum to a national of another Member State on grounds of alleged political persecution implicitly calls into question the independence of that Member State’s judiciary and risks undermining mutual trust and the principle of sincere cooperation under Article 4(3) TEU. Against this background: 1.
Is the Commission in contact with the Hungarian authorities regarding this case, and how does it assess the admissibility of such an asylum claim under EU law?
What impact does the Commission consider this decision may have on the EU legal order and judicial cooperation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.4.2026) The Commission does not comment or intervene in individual cases. Under EU law, the examination of applications for international protection is the responsibility of the Member States.

If the applicant is an EU citizen, their application can be declared admissible by another Member State only in very exceptional circumstances listed under Protocol 24 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU1. The level of protection of fundamental rights and freedoms in all Member States is such that all Member States are considered safe countries in relation to asylum matters.
1 Consolidated version of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union - Protocols – Protocol (No 24) on
asylum for nationals of Member States of the European Union Official Journal 115, 09.05.2008 pp. 0305 – 0306.
